note: To feel comfortable doing something you arguably shouldn't. You mostly hear it as an accusation, 你还好意思说, where the shame someone ought to feel is the whole point.
A warm feeling toward someone or something. When you say 我对他有好感, it's often a shy way of admitting you like them.
A gated residential compound of apartment blocks. You picture the guard at the gate, shared courtyards and old people on benches, a more enclosed world than a neighbourhood.
The very bottom of society or a company. 底层 sounds heavy: you picture migrant workers and long hours, and 从底层做起 means you earned your way up.
Everything a job gives you: pay, benefits and standing together. When you ask 待遇怎么样, you want the whole package, not only the salary.
Pleased with yourself and showing it. There's a slight disapproval in it: you picture a smug grin, and 得意忘形 warns you what comes next.
To get on someone's wrong side. You fear it more than the word suggests, because 得罪人 can cost you favours and connections for years.
Afraid of being found out because you know you're in the wrong. You feel hollow, 虚, in the chest, and you can't quite meet anyone's eye.
Courier delivery, the pulse of daily online shopping. You picture a pickup code on your phone, parcel lockers by the gate and riders racing their e-bikes.
A bad mood or a sulk over something. When someone 闹情绪 at work, you know they're upset and making it felt, and nobody needs to name the feeling.
To look someone up and down. You feel it when it happens to you: a slow, assessing look that decides what kind of person you are.
To argue back and forth and pass the blame, getting nowhere. You picture departments shoving a problem at each other while your matter sits unsolved.
To check in formally with an organisation on your first day. You picture a new school or work unit, signing in at a desk and being told where you belong.
To open up to the outside. You can't hear it without 改革开放, the reforms from 1978 that changed your parents' lives and the whole country.
Relaxed about sex. Saying 她很开放 can be neutral or admiring, but you may also hear a judgement in it, so it depends who's talking.
